title: Prune redundant CUDA/driver symbols to slim runtime image and reduce kernel probe flakiness
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Why: Our runtime images and live kernel probe path are suffering from two related problems: (1) shared-object symbol bloat increases image size and slows startup, and (2) noisy symbol resolution during GPU kernel probing causes transient failures and probe jitter on heterogeneous fleets. This ticket scopes a targeted refactor and packaging pipeline changes to identify and prune redundant CUDA and vendor driver symbols while preserving ABI compatibility for loaded plugins (CUTLASS/Triton/quant kernels).

What we'll do:
- Inventory exported symbols from our runtime and bundled vendor libraries (libcuda, libcudart, custom quant kernels).
- Build a symbol whitelist/compat-shim approach: keep only symbols used by our runtime and known plugins; stub or remove the rest using objcopy/strip and version scripts.
- Introduce a deterministic symbol-stripping step in the GPU artifact packaging job and produce a "compat" symbol manifest per bundle.
- Add lightweight runtime stubs for a small set of driver-facing APIs that some third-party kernels probe for (to avoid runtime link-time failures).
- Add CI smoke and canary benchmarks that run kernel probing and warmup flows on a hetero-GPU matrix to validate no regressions.

Non-goals: Full ABI reimplementation for vendor drivers or replacing vendor shared objects. This is a packaging/compat shim effort only.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Packaged runtime artifacts are at least 20% smaller (MB) compared to current baseline for the same build matrix without affecting known workloads.
2) Kernel probe median latency on staging clusters reduces by >= 25ms on average across the hetero GPU matrix.
3) No new probe-time OOMs or symbol lookup failures in 48h canary runs.
4) CI smoke tests covering canary workloads pass in our cross-GPU matrix.
5) Rollout plan exists and feature flag gating completed.
success_metrics:
- Image size reduction (MB) measured per artifact: baseline vs pruned.
- Kernel probe latency p50/p95 (ms) before/after on staging (per instance type).
- Number of probe-related incidents (weekly) drops to zero for canary tenants.
- Percentage of quant/kernel plugins that require shim changes (target < 5%).
risks:
- Over-stripping symbols could break third-party kernel plugins leading to immediate failures.
- Some vendor drivers rely on weak/undocumented symbols; shimming may miss edge cases.
- Packaging step adds complexity and longer build times; may upset release cadence if not optimized.
- CI matrix coverage may miss rare GPU/driver combos; must canary gradually.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Spike + CI integration (this ticket). Build pruned artifacts and run internal smoke tests.
Phase 2: Staged canary against non-critical tenants in staging region with telemetry enabled for 72h.
Phase 3: Roll forward to limited production subset (dedicated pools) with automatic rollback on error thresholds.
Phase 4: Full rollout across Dedicated fleets after 1 week of stable metrics.
Feature gating: packaging on/off via build flag; runtime looks up compat manifest and loads stubs only if present.
test_plan:
- Unit: symbol inventory tooling unit tests (node/python).
- Integration: CI job that builds pruned artifact and bootstraps runtime in a containerized hetero-GPU emulator (QEMU-based smoke).
- Performance: end-to-end probe + warmup trace comparing baseline and pruned artifact across 3 GPU types (A100, H100, T4).
- Canary: 72h canary with real traffic and synthetic load; automated alerting on increased probe latency, OOMs, or plugin errors.
